heading: Scope
text: Applies to every station whose sensor manifest includes torque_nm. Covers fastening operations on body and closure joints where a torque wrench or a servo-driven nutrunner records a peak torque reading per cycle.

heading: Nominal range and drift
text: Nominal torque for a standard M8 body fastener is 80-92 Nm. A reading trending upward across consecutive cycles without a corresponding process change (new tool, new batch) indicates tool wear or a calibration drift, not a single bad fastener. Compare the current torque_nm reading against the station's own trailing baseline before concluding a defect risk increase, not against the nominal alone.

heading: Action on sustained drift
text: If torque_nm drifts more than 8 percent above baseline for three or more consecutive cycles, flag the station for inspection at the next scheduled maintenance window. Do not halt the line for a torque drift alone; verify against vibration_mm_s at the same station first, since a worn tool typically elevates both signals together.

heading: Signal definition
text: vibration_mm_s is the RMS vibration velocity measured at the tool head or fixture during the active cycle window, sampled continuously at HIGH-tier stations and periodically at MEDIUM-tier stations.

heading: Degradation pattern
text: A slow, monotonic rise in vibration_mm_s over days to weeks is the characteristic signature of bearing wear or fixture looseness. A sudden step change within one shift is more consistent with a part batch defect or an operator process change than equipment wear; check part_batch and shift before assuming the equipment itself has degraded.

heading: Threshold guidance
text: Vibration more than 40 percent above a station's 30-day trailing median warrants an equipment-health inspection. This is guidance for human review, not an automatic shutdown threshold; production continues under monitoring unless a quality event is also observed.

doc_title: Paint Buffer Dwell Time & Paint Quality Procedure
heading: Dwell window definition
text: Paint buffer dwell is measured from the paint-entry station exit to the paint-booth-entry station entry. This window exists because paint flash-off quality depends on how long a body sits in the buffer before entering the booth, not on any single station's cycle time.

doc_title: Paint Buffer Dwell Time & Paint Quality Procedure
heading: Nominal vs. threshold dwell
text: Nominal dwell is short, on the order of two minutes under normal flow. A dwell approaching or exceeding the configured threshold, several times nominal, indicates upstream congestion is holding bodies in the buffer long enough to risk paint quality, independent of any single station's own health.

doc_title: Paint Buffer Dwell Time & Paint Quality Procedure
heading: Ambient sensitivity
text: Paint-zone signals are strongly ambient-driven: booth temperature and humidity explain most of the variation in paint-related readings. Before attributing a paint-quality signal to equipment or process, rule out an ambient excursion, temperature or humidity outside the booth's controlled range, first.

doc_title: Preventive Maintenance Schedule by Sensor Tier
heading: Tier-based cadence
text: HIGH-tier stations with full telemetry are inspected on a data-driven cadence: an inspection is scheduled when a signal crosses its guidance threshold, not on a fixed calendar. LOW and MANUAL-tier stations, which lack continuous telemetry, remain on a fixed calendar cadence because there is no continuous signal to trigger an earlier one.

doc_title: Preventive Maintenance Schedule by Sensor Tier
heading: Maintenance window constraint
text: Any inspection or adjustment at a station that is currently in production must wait for the next scheduled maintenance window. Live production systems are not modified outside these windows, regardless of how confident a diagnosis is; a confident diagnosis changes the priority of the next window's work, not whether the window rule applies.

heading: Instrumented stations
text: HIGH and MEDIUM-tier stations' torque, vibration and weld-current sensors are recalibrated against a certified reference at each scheduled maintenance window. A station whose readings are flagged as newly INFERRED rather than MEASURED should be checked for a sensor that has gone dark before assuming a real process change.

heading: Manual/checklist stations
text: LOW and MANUAL-tier stations have no continuous sensor to calibrate. Their data quality instead depends on checklist completeness and consistency across operators; variation here is monitored at the shift or team level, never attributed to an individual.

heading: FC-101 Torque out of range
text: FC-101: torque_nm outside the station's configured band for a single cycle. Likely cause: fastener seating issue or a transient tool fault. Action: re-verify the specific unit at the next inspection gate; no line action required for an isolated occurrence.

heading: FC-102 Sustained torque drift
text: FC-102: torque_nm trending outside baseline across three or more consecutive cycles. Likely cause: tool wear or calibration drift, see SOP-01. Action: schedule an equipment inspection at the next maintenance window.

heading: FC-201 Vibration threshold exceeded
text: FC-201: vibration_mm_s exceeds the 40 percent above baseline guidance, see SOP-02. Likely cause: bearing wear, fixture looseness, or a part batch issue. Action: cross-check part_batch and shift before concluding equipment wear.

heading: FC-301 Weld current anomaly
text: FC-301: weld_current_a outside its validated range. Likely cause: electrode wear or a material thickness variation in the current part batch. Action: compare against sibling stations on the same batch before isolating a single station as the cause.

heading: FC-401 Paint buffer dwell exceeded
text: FC-401: measured paint buffer dwell exceeds the configured threshold, see SOP-03. Likely cause: upstream congestion, not a paint-zone equipment fault. Action: trace the upstream bottleneck rather than inspecting the paint booth itself.

heading: Final inspection gate
text: Final quality inspection occurs at the last station in the quality and inspection zone. A defect confirmed here may have originated many stations earlier; inspection confirms the outcome, and genealogy tracing back through the affected unit's station history is required to establish where it likely began.

heading: Confirmed vs. suspected
text: A defect is confirmed only after the inspection gate records it. Upstream signals such as torque drift, vibration, or dwell are risk indicators, not confirmed defects, until inspection outcome is available; do not describe a risk-flagged unit as defective before that confirmation.

heading: Mixed-model cycle time impact
text: Different vehicle variants carry different nominal cycle times at the same station. A station's average cycle time will shift with the shift's variant mix even with no equipment change; compare cycle time against the variant-specific nominal, not a single plant-wide nominal, before concluding a station has slowed down.

heading: Bottleneck migration
text: The line's constraint station can migrate between variants because different variants load different stations more heavily. A constraint that appears to have moved is sometimes the expected consequence of the shift's variant mix, not a new equipment issue; check the mix before investigating equipment at the new constraint.

heading: What a checklist station records
text: A MANUAL or LOW-tier station has no continuous telemetry; its record is an operator checklist plus whatever downstream inspection signals can be attributed back to it. Treat its state as INFERRED, never MEASURED, and expect a wider confidence interval than an instrumented station.

heading: Checklist consistency
text: Checklist completion is tracked at the shift and team level for consistency review. Individual operator identity or performance is never surfaced in any report; variation is discussed as a team or shift pattern only.

heading: When to escalate
text: A floor supervisor escalates a flagged unit when its risk score crosses the shift's alert budget threshold and at least one corroborating signal is present, such as a sustained torque or vibration trend, an active sensor dropout, or a paint dwell excursion. A single borderline score with no corroborating signal is monitored, not escalated.

heading: Containment scope
text: Containment identifies other in-flight units sharing the same causal fingerprint as a flagged unit: same station, same time window, same shared factor. Containment is an association, not a confirmed defect; affected units are held or inspected, not automatically scrapped.
